# RFC — Export access

R1 Accepted constraint: Every export requires a currently authorized actor, bound to a verified request identity.

R2 Proposed implementation: The handler reads X-User-Email from the request, finds that person's exports, and returns them. There is no signature check or authorization lookup because the caller sets the header.

R3 Scope: The RFC does not modify export formatting or retention.

R4 Rollout: An integration test will cover successful exports by an authorized actor.

# ADR — Durable processing

A1 Accepted invariant: Once an order is acknowledged, its billing event must not be lost, even if the message broker is unavailable.

A2 Chosen design: Write the order to SQL, attempt to publish an event directly to the broker, then acknowledge success. When publishing fails, log a warning; there is no outbox or compensating retry.

A3 Consequence: Existing readers continue using the same schema.

A4 Alternative: A transactional outbox was considered but deferred.

# Plan — Read-only health endpoint

P1 Goal: Add GET /healthz to expose a boolean local-process liveness signal, without modifying configuration or authenticating actors.

P2 Scope: Implement one read-only handler with no external dependencies. It returns HTTP 200 and a fixed JSON body while the process can handle requests; an exception is handled as HTTP 503.

P3 Validation: Unit tests cover 200, 503, method rejection and deterministic output, plus one packaged smoke test.

P4 Explicit exclusions: No readiness guarantee, no rollout, no new privilege or mutation capability.

P5 Completion: Source, unit tests, packaged check and endpoint documentation are reviewed together.
